anomalies.observed: The net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW contains only the anodes of D4, D14, and D23; no supply pin, driver output, or other source is connected to that net.
anomalies.expected: An LED power net named /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW should be connected to a 3.3 V source or to the driven LED-power net (for example /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV / U34.4) so that the Ethernet and activity LEDs can light. Standard practice requires LED anodes to be tied to a defined supply or driver.

anomalies.impact: D4, D14, and D23 will remain dark because their anodes are floating; Ethernet link/activity indication and the associated Pi activity LED will not behave as intended.

anomalies.observed: GND1 and GND2 of both isolated CAN transceivers are connected to the same system GND net.
anomalies.expected: For isolated CAN transceivers, GND1 (logic side) and GND2 (bus side) should be separate ground nets to preserve galvanic isolation. The specification describes two isolated CAN buses implemented through isolated CAN transceivers.

anomalies.impact: The CAN transceiver isolation barrier is defeated; the CAN buses are not isolated from system ground as intended, which can allow ground loops and removes the expected isolation behavior.

parsed.summary: The design files contain at least one clear anomaly: the /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW net is unpowered, leaving D4/D14/D23 LEDs non-functional. A second likely deviation is that the isolated CAN transceivers have GND1 and GND2 tied to system ground, defeating the intended CAN isolation.
